_comment: First-playable roster from the design doc Creatures tab (Floeback deferred to Full release, design review #14). Health/damage default to the zone tier's starting numbers; speeds, sizes, colours, foods and products are placeholders. taming: methods allowed for this creature only (design review #16). attacks: special moves besides the bite (lunge, charge, spit, stomp; numbers in tuning.json creatureAI). diet: carnivore / herbivore / lithovore (default from its food; carnivores hunt smaller non-carnivores when hungry). activity: diurnal (sleeps at night) / nocturnal (sleeps by day) / any. pack: [smallest, largest] pack on the island, mostly small (WRWildlife); wanderChance: the share of its packs that travel far.

creatures._why: The tundra's road over cold water (Raven: carries a rider through icy water). It hauls out on the shore ice of the tundra coast and fishes the shallows, so you meet it where the land meets the Rime Sound; passive, it slips into the sea when threatened. A crust of sea ice has grown over its back: that's where a rider sits (cooks/build-taming.md 2.5).
creatures.name: Floeback

creatures._why: SKY 2.9: a lean pale-dun stag 1.8 m at the shoulder with four feathered wings (biplane, Microraptor: long fore-wings from the shoulders 6 m across, shorter hind-wings from the thighs), swept bone-pale antlers with dark tips like a dead tree, a long silver-white mane that streams. Herds of 2-4 on the W3 Mane Ledges; they graze the W2 and W1 islands at dawn; they defend herd and eggs together. Tamed from a stolen egg: the first flying mount. The Frostantler rig with the wings, mane and antler tips modelled on its bones (WRSkyCreatures).
creatures.name: Windmane

creatures._bosses: Bosses tab. Health comes from enemies.majorBossSolo / miniBossSolo (scaled by party size); attacks and counterplay are in WRBoss.cpp, numbers in tuning.json bosses.*. loot = what each player who dealt >= 10% gets.

creatures.name: Cinderhorn
creatures._why: The Emberhorn herd's old bull: the ash plains are flat and open, the only ground where a 25 m charge reads and can be baited into the basalt columns along his loop.

creatures.name: Old Tusker
creatures._why: The drudge herd's bull on the snow flats: he walks the frozen ground between the herds; set burning, he rolls the fire out in the deep snow (no open water within reach of the flats).

creatures._storm: Storm peaks (cooks/biome-lightning.md 2.9-2.11; cooks/build-biome-lightning.md 1.3): stand-in rigs with their own palette (look.tint over M_CreatureTint) and code-modelled silhouette parts (look.kind, WRStormCreatures.cpp); behaviour beyond the rows in WRStormCreatures / WRStormBosses. lootChance: drops by chance (into the killer's bag). climbSlope / jumpHeight: a mount's climbing; senseOre cm (Coilburrow); scoutMark cm (Stormkite); strikeGround cm (Rodcrest, read by the strike); noGust (Galeback).

creatures.name: The Bellwether
creatures._why: The belled lead ram the Rodwardens set over their flocks: he walks his 2.6 km loop of ridges and cliff paths (storm_peaks.json bellwether) with his herd, sleeps at the fold by night.

creatures._swamp: The Swamp (cooks/biome-swamp.md 2.12; cooks/build-biome-swamp.md 2.6): stand-in rigs with the cook's palette (look.tint over M_CreatureTint) and code-built silhouette parts (look.kind, WRSwampCreatures.cpp); behaviour beyond the rows in WRSwampCreatures. Every swamp creature ignores bleedwater, quag and marsh gas (resists). look.flatten cm: the body squashed to this height after the fit (the Murkjaw's low wedge; strides unchanged). wadeDepth cm: walks the bottom in water up to this deep (Mudhulk 250, Mirestrider 140). riderPasses: hazards its rider ignores while mounted. findSites cm (Bogsnout): bog bodies, caches and the Coven chimney marked for its owner; gatherBoost {item: [mult, cm]} near its owner. pouch: a light tame rides its owner's shoulder while they swim. Taming method blood_ritual: the Murkjaw's blood-path rite (E at its mouth, 4 s, 10+ Blood points).

creatures.name: Murkjaw
creatures._why: The swamp's apex: a 7 m saltwater-croc body with a false-gharial bar of teeth splayed outside the closed jaw, osteoderms grown over with bloodmoss, red tapetum eyeshine. It waits under the duckweed (WRSwampCreatures ambush) and bursts out at whatever comes within 7 m of the water.

creatures.name: Young Murkjaw
creatures._why: A Murkjaw not yet grown (cook 2.12.3: M1 at night, only at the channel mouths, 120 HP, midland tier): the same body, teeth and eyeshine at a little over half the size.

creatures.name: Gorgeleech
creatures._why: A medicinal leech at dog size: the Y-shaped three-jawed sucker, ten eyes in a crescent, a ribbon swim and an inchworm loop on land. Packs latch on and drain (WRSwampCreatures latch), up to three on one survivor, one a limb.

creatures.name: Vharra, Queen of the Mire
creatures._why: The leech-drake of the Mother's Throat (cooks/biome-swamp.md 2.14): a drake's front (the MountainDragon rig with its hind legs, tail, wings and head hidden) on a ringed leech trunk tapering 18 m to the sucker disc that anchors her to the west wall; the three-plate hood that splits into a radial three-jawed mouth; ten dull-red eyes; three blood sacs that fill as she drains. Glossy black-olive with paired rust stripes. Weak to Lightning; bleed builds on her at half. The look and the fight are WRSwampVharra.cpp.

creatures.name: Vharra's brood
creatures._why: Gorgeleech young Vharra sheds from her split sacs into the pool (cook 2.14 Brood shed): 25 HP, they go for the furthest tame first and latch on. Only ever out in her fight (WRSwampVharra.cpp spawns them).

creatures.name: Latch leech
creatures._why: The Red Tide's swarm (cook 2.8 leech boil, 2.12.2 swarm row): finger-long leeches that come up out of bleedwater two at a time onto whoever wades it. 25 HP; they latch, drain and bleed you until knocked off.

creatures.name: Hexcrow
creatures._why: A raven of 2.4 m span with a rook's bare bone-white face and a crest of ragged hackles; murders that curse with their cry, rake from the air and peck at whatever is down. Circling Hexcrows over the reeds mean something is dying there.

creatures.name: Bogstalker
creatures._why: An Argentine horned frog at bull size: a mound that is mostly mouth, horned brows, a pale throat that pumps twice before the tongue. It pulls you in and swallows you whole (WRSwampCreatures tongue and gulp).

creatures.name: Mirestrider
creatures._why: A flightless stilt bird 3.5 m tall with a shoebill's head and bill, a heron's neck and a jacana's splayed toes. It stands for minutes in the shallows and stabs fish; hit one and the bill-clatter turns the whole herd. Tamed, it is the swamp's mount: full speed through quag and water to 1.4 m, and its rider never touches the bleedwater.

creatures.name: Mudhulk
creatures._why: A hippo of the bog: a barrel body, a box of a head with short tusks, skin that sweats red (the real hippo's blood sweat). Its yawn is the warning; its charge stops at nothing but a trunk. Tamed it hauls 600 and walks the bottom of anything up to 2.5 m deep.

creatures.name: Bogsnout
creatures._why: A babirusa on a truffle-hog body: two tusks curl up through the snout and back over its face. It roots out what the bog keeps (bog bodies, buried caches, the Coven's chimney) and doubles the bloodmoss you pick near it.

creatures.name: Lanterntoad
creatures._why: A cane toad with a throat sac that glows gold-green; they sit in rings at night and trill in turn. Startled, one puffs a flash in your face and hops off. Tamed it lights 10 m round its owner and rides a shoulder pouch through the water.

creatures.name: Reedfowl
creatures._why: A purple swamphen a metre tall: blue-purple with a red shield on the brow, long toes for walking the lily pads. Flocks graze the reed flats; cornered, one pecks and runs.

creatures.name: Mother Maw
creatures._why: The Murkjaw matriarch (cook 2.13.1, Jenny Greenteeth): 13 m, broad as a punt, her snout scarred white, a living mat of duckweed and bloodmoss on her back so she lies like a floating island; old arrows and a Coven bone hook in her neck plates. Her nest pool is ringed by the broken boardwalk square (WRSwampBosses): on the planks she has to rear, belly open; her slams break sections; you mend them with 2 wood in 3 s; fire on the nest draws her out 8 s; young at 60% and 30%.

creatures.name: The Hex-Warden
creatures._why: The last Coven witch (cook 2.13.2; bolotnik call-mimicry, the Morrigan's crows): ageless, kept young by blood, tall and lean and moving like a dancer; crow-skull mask, a long cloak of black crow feathers that flares into wings, a bone-and-leather corset, garnet vein-rings on bare arms, a bone sickle in each hand. Four fetish totems on her Ossuary give her curses (crow: scatter; bone: curse on her sickles; blood: heals on bleeds; voice: the mimic call). Her mask breaks on a stance break. On the Red Tide's nights she walks the boardwalks and hexes the beasts round her.

creatures.name: Fetish totem
creatures._why: One of the Hex-Warden's four fetish totems (crow, bone, blood, voice) on the Ossuary's shoulders: the hit body standing in its pole (the pole is the arena prop). 400 HP, x2 from blunt (physResist) and fire (WRSwampBosses). Breaking one strips its curse for the fight and staggers her if she's within 15 m. In no spawn region: she raises them.

creatures.name: The Bloat
creatures._why: A Gorgeleech swollen to 6 m (cook 2.13.3; salt on a leech): skin stretched thin enough that the stolen blood shows, dark at rest and bright garnet gorged; ten eyes, stripes pulled wide apart, three veins standing proud. It walks its 3.5 km loop from the Wallow (swamp.json arenas.bloat.route) at night and sleeps there by day; drains Mudhulks; walks the Drowned Causeway on the Red Tide; leads the Blood invasions. Its gorge meter is its body (WRSwampBosses): salt makes it vomit, fire and frost keep it low; at 100% it bursts.

creatures.name: Slimeshell
creatures._why: An apple snail a metre long: a banded coiled shell on a grey gliding foot; it lays bright pink clutches on the reeds (the World kit's egg reeds). It never attacks; touched, it pulls into the shell.

creatures.name: Hollowfang
creatures._why: The Void's pack hunter (biome-void 2.12.1): a Black Shuck at greyhound-plus size, deep chest and tucked waist, a hairless hide so tight the ribs and spine show, an eyeless elongated skull with two deep pits, black glass teeth past the lips. It blinks 4-6 m to your flank (a shudder and a hard reversed breath first, a lensing ripple where it will arrive) and still winds up every bite in full.

creatures.name: Riftmaw
creatures._why: A sea-lamprey ring mouth split into four hooked jaw-plates on a crocodile's forelimbs and belly armour, its eel tail never leaving the rift (biome-void 2.12.1). It lies in a large rift's tear and bursts out of any rift within 8 m; more than 30 m from a rift it fights on land, slowed, and can't go back: luring it away is the skill.

creatures.name: Nullwing
creatures._why: A lammergeier frame and bare neck on fruit-bat wing membranes, a toothed beak; its torn membranes show the void through the holes (biome-void 2.12.1). It banks wide and lays a black void ribbon across your route, dives, and spits void that never homes.

creatures.name: Gnawer
creatures._why: A naked mole-rat at 40 cm: wrinkled, hairless, pink-grey, tiny eyes and two long orange-yellow chisel incisors outside the lips, pouring out of a warren in dozens (biome-void 2.12.1). It latches and eats your max health; a roll or a hit shakes every one off.

creatures.name: The Hush
creatures._why: An aye-aye scaled to 3.2 m: huge mobile ear fans, a long skeletal tapping finger, digitigrade legs and an emaciated knuckle-walking stance, eyeless (biome-void 2.12.1). Blind: it hunts by noise. It rises to listen (ears unfold with a leathery snap, two taps of the long finger): your cue to stop.

creatures.name: Voidstrider
creatures._why: A gaunt Akhal-Teke horse at 2.4 m, its face hairless and skull-tight, a mane and tail of fine black filaments that drift as if underwater (biome-void 2.12.1). Ridden it sprints 1,350 and blinks 5 m every 8 s (Dodge); it walks rift zones unhurt.

creatures.name: Riftback
creatures._why: A glyptodont's domed shell on a sloth's long-clawed forelimbs; the shell's top is split by a lens-shaped seam where space folds (biome-void 2.12.1). Tamed, its pocket opens your clan's Rift chest network: an ender chest on legs. Offer it voidglass, approaching slowly.

creatures.name: Driftmote
creatures._why: A moon-jelly bell with comb-jelly light rows and trailing filaments, floating 1-3 m up on voidglass grit in its bell (the floating rule; biome-void 2.12.1). Tamed it senses rifts, hidden caches, hollow crust and Rift Storm seeds within 30 m, pulsing faster as it closes in (0.5 Hz at 30 m to 3 Hz at 3 m).

creatures.name: Withergoat
creatures._why: A Valais-type goat with long drooping ears and four horns (a Jacob sheep's), a dull grey coat that sheds like ash, gold goat-pupil eyes (biome-void 2.12.1). The Wasteland's farm animal: milk and hide, fed ashen grain; herds flee litter fire.

creatures.name: The Unravelled
creatures._why: Station 1, the Cantor's Stair (biome-void 2.13.1): a 3.4 m Choir cantor held apart, head, ribs, pelvis and limbs separate pieces of grey bone and stone moving as one, a fist-sized voidglass heart in the open ribs, a 3 m iron tuning-staff. Hits on the body take x0.3; after 300 damage or a heavy blow it unravels into a whirling column, travels 8-15 m and reforms: for the first 0.6 s the core hangs alone (x3, stance x4), then the pieces snap shut (Reform slam). WRVoidBosses.

creatures.name: Mother of Rifts
creatures._why: Station 2, the Rift Pens (biome-void 2.13.2): a Riftmaw matriarch 9 m long, her front half out of a 12 m lair rift, her back studded with small tears; four door-sized jaw-plates, scarred belly plates. She opens brood rifts in the six pens (Gnawer swarms or a Hollowfang every 15 s, up to 4); a brood rift has 400 HP or closes to thrown anchor salt; all closed: the strain stuns her 4 s. WRVoidBosses.

creatures.name: The Starving One
creatures._why: Station 3, the Alms House (biome-void 2.13.3): a 5 m emaciated giant, a gorilla's knuckle-walking frame starved to skin over rib and hip, a hyena's sloping back, a jaw that unhinges to its chest. Every blow or grab that lands eats one of your buffs and it grows (+10% size, damage; +5% speed; 5 stacks); food dropped or thrown within 15 m draws it to eat for 2.5 s (backstab stance on it), each eaten taking a stack off. WRVoidBosses.

creatures.name: The Null Warden
creatures._why: Station 4, the Null Gate (biome-void 2.13.4): a 4.2 m Choir gate-guard in voidglass plate over grey skin, a closed bell-shaped helm, a 2 m black bronze bell on a chain and a long iron key-halberd. A null field 12 m round him: spells fizzle (half their cost back), projectiles drop dead; melee only. His key holds the Null Gate's lock bar (AWRNullGate). WRVoidBosses.

creatures.name: The Echo
creatures._why: Roaming (biome-void 2.13.5): a lanky 3.6 m biped on a lyrebird's display tail and a raven's beak-skull, a 4 m fan of mirror-black plumes. It walks a 2.4 km loop through the Rift Fields and the Gauntlet Road by night and rests on the Glass Sea by day. It mimics the last path ability that hit it (your colour and sound reversed in the plumes, 1.0 s); three different ones in a row and its Mimic fails: stunned 2 s. WRVoidBosses.

creatures.name: Vorhollow, the Devouring Dark
creatures._why: The Wasteland's major boss (biome-void 2.14): what the Choir's singing fed. 8.5 m at the shoulder on all fours, 13 m reared, 24 m with the tail of 14 floating vertebrae; aye-aye forelimbs ending in 1.8 m voidglass hooks; a blunt eyeless head that splits into four jaw-petals round a lamprey ring; a 4 m hole straight through its chest showing a lensed starfield; grey skin cracked like dry clay, black-violet in the cracks, voidglass spines. It sits on the Choir's last stage, an island chained over the Great Rift (AWRVorhollowStage). WRVoidBosses.

creatures.name: Brood rift
creatures._why: A small tear the Mother of Rifts opens in one of her pens (WRVoidBosses): it spits Gnawers or a Hollowfang every 15 s until closed: 400 damage, or thrown anchor salt. Drawn as a tear; the moth rig is hidden.

creatures.name: The Void heart
creatures._why: Vorhollow's heart, hanging from cords in the Gullet (biome-void 2.14.2 phase 3): hits on it count x1.5 on Vorhollow's shared health (WRVoidBosses). Drawn in code; the moth rig is hidden.

creatures.name: Rift heart
creatures._why: A storm rift's heart (biome-void 2.10): a 1.5 m voidglass core floating at the tear's centre. Break it to close the rift (void x0.5; thrown anchor salt -300). WRVoidHazards.

creatures._forest: The Ancient forest (cooks/biome-forest.md 2.12; cooks/build-biome-forest.md 1.3, 2.9): stand-in rigs with the cook's palette (look.tint over M_CreatureTint) and code-modelled silhouette parts (look.kind, WRForestCreatures.cpp), behaviour beyond the rows in WRForestCreatures. Rig picks: Mossmaul on Rimeclaw (long-legged maned cat body, the hump and hooked claws modelled), Thornlynx on Pale_hunter (lean wolf-leopard, flattened and lengthened to a low cat), Rootcoil on Glacimaw (the flat ringed worm, flattened to a 60 cm body and stretched to 12 m: the head becomes a viper's wedge), Bramblewasp on Kilnmite (six-legged insect), Elderelk and Dappledoe on Frostantler, Burlbeast on Emberhorn, Truffler on Pumicehog, Hiveback on Glowmoth (narrowed wings, the fur barrel modelled), Fernsheep on Woolly_drudge (as the Puffram), Glimmerfinch on Snowpuff (the lead bird; its flock modelled round it). Every forest creature ignores thornbrakes and leaf pits (resists). look.flatten cm: the drawn body squashed to this height; look.stretch: the drawn body lengthened along its spine (strides unchanged). jumpHeight cm (the Elderelk clears 2 m). haulDrag: heartwood a tamed Burlbeast drags home a game day. Taming path_magic on the Mossmaul is the Nature path's hold-Interact calm (4 s, 10+ Nature points, 40 Growth), not the element-hit calm.

creatures.name: Mossmaul
creatures._why: The old-growth's apex: a short-faced bear's long legs and huge shoulder hump with a ground sloth's three hooked 35 cm claws, walking on its knuckles; a living mat of moss, fern and shelf fungus grows over the hump and spine. Its roar shakes the widowmakers loose; it hugs, it hammers down, it rushes into trunks. A sow keeps a larder of Burlbeast under moss (WRForestCreatures).

creatures.name: Thornlynx
creatures._why: A clouded leopard 2.4 m long: the longest canines of any cat for its size, a lynx's ear tufts grown into black spikes, grey-gold with dark cloud blotches. It climbs trunks head-first and hangs over trails, dropping on what passes under; hurt below 40% it goes back up the nearest trunk (WRForestCreatures).

creatures.name: Rootcoil
creatures._why: A reticulated python's length with an anaconda's bulk at 12 m, keeled scales like bark, moss saddles, heat pits along the lips. Lying still it is a fallen log among the roots, breathing slowly; within 7 m the head lifts and strikes, and the coils come for you (WRForestCreatures log rest and constrict).

creatures.name: Bramblewasp
creatures._why: A Japanese giant hornet at fist size: an orange head with heavy mandibles, a black-and-amber banded abdomen, a stinger as long as a finger. Swarms of 6 to 12 pour out of the paper nests (WRForestHazards); scouts mark a body with pheromone and every wasp within 40 m comes for it (water or smoke washes it off). The wandering pairs in the spawn tables are scouts. 25 HP: any one or two hits.

creatures.name: Elderelk
creatures._why: An Irish elk's build: 2.1 m at the shoulder under palmate antlers 3.6 m across, hung with ivy and moss. Hit one and it bugles, and the herd within 40 m turns on you. Tamed it is the forest's fastest mount: a thin body that slips between trunks, a 2 m leap over fallen giants, and it walks through thornbrakes with its rider.

creatures.name: Burlbeast
creatures._why: A gaur or an aurochs: a massive humped wild ox 2 m at the shoulder whose back and shoulders carry ridged keratin plates with the colour and grain of bark burls; white stockings. Its stomp, sweep and crash carry hyperarmor. Offered heartwood it comes to you; tamed it hauls 300, makes heartwood come away x1.25 within 15 m, and drags a fallen giant's log home once a game day.

creatures.name: Truffler
creatures._why: A Eurasian wild boar 1.2 m long with a long flexible rooting snout, short tusks and a bristle crest. Tamed it noses out truffles, buried caches and the leaf pits (it snorts at them), digs the Hollow Root's soft spot open and turns up forest seeds.

creatures.name: Hiveback
creatures._why: A bumblebee a metre long: dense black and amber fur, a round body, short blurring wings, pollen baskets on its legs. Three to six keep each hive and sting only near it or when hit; on Bramblewasps (and on a survivor robbing the hive) they heat-ball: several converge and cling, each slowing you 10%, a roll knocks one off, fire knocks them all off. Raised from a stolen egg it lives in a beehive piece.

creatures.name: Fernsheep
creatures._why: A primitive heath sheep (Soay-like) whose fleece grows in curls like fern fiddleheads, moss-green when wet; a dark face and swept amber horns. Flocks graze the meadows; cornered, one butts and runs.

creatures.name: Dappledoe
creatures._why: A fallow deer: a chestnut coat with white spots, a black-edged white rump, a tail always flicking, palmate antlers on the bucks. At night groups bed down in rings in the meadows (a sneak-tame window); Thornlynx drop on them at dusk.

creatures.name: Glimmerfinch
creatures._why: A goldfinch body with a hummingbird's hover and an iridescent throat, in flocks of 6 to 20 (one creature is one flock: the lead bird and its flock round it). Flocks lift over any fresh kill or ripe patch, a sign seen from 300 m. Tamed (offer seeds) the flock pollinates crops within 20 m (x0.85 time) and, when you whistle, lifts and circles over the nearest ripe wild plant or hive within 60 m. It never attacks.

creatures._forest_bosses: The Ancient forest's bosses (cooks/biome-forest.md 2.13-2.14; cooks/build-biome-forest.md 2.10; WRForestBosses.cpp, looks in WRForestBossLook.cpp): each the closest real rig at its size with the cook's palette (look.tint over M_CreatureTint) and code-built parts (look.kind). Moves are attacks.json bosses rows; their counters (bark plates, combs, walkways, the herd and the snares, the root lines) are code with numbers in tuning bosses.<id>. The arenas (forest.json arenas) place Old Gnarl, the Bramblequeen, the Grey Matron and Sylvaroth (UWRForestArenas); the Hornwarden walks his roam loop (forest.json route 'hornwarden', copied here in cm) with his herd of Elderelk.

creatures.name: Old Gnarl
creatures._why: An awakened oak 18 m tall that walks on its roots like a crouched giant (the Elder Mother): the newcomers' clear-cut woke it, their axes are still in its legs. Strip its bark (axes) and burn the pale wood.

creatures.name: The Bramblequeen
creatures._why: A Bramblewasp queen 4 m long in the Paper Hollow (the giant hornet colony): she flies the hive's open middle between its three paper floors and calls her swarm from the brood combs. Break the combs, smoke the hive, bring Hivebacks.

creatures.name: The Grey Matron
creatures._why: A Thornlynx matriarch 4 m long gone grey-blue with age (Black Annis' Bower): she keeps to the six oaks' walkways and drops on you from them; cut the walkways' rope anchors and she comes down on her old leg.

creatures.name: The Hornwarden
creatures._why: An Elderelk bull 4.5 m at the shoulder under an 8 m crown hung with banner rags (Herne): he walks a 3.2 km loop through the meadows and the streams with his herd, rests at the Antler Barrow at noon, stands under the Hanging Oak at dusk, drinks at Herne's Ford at nightfall. Never hurt the herd; roots hold him. He leads the Wild Hunt on the Bloom's night.

creatures.name: Sylvaroth, the World-Root
creatures._why: A strangler-fig titan in the Clearing of Four Hearts: a lattice of roots fused into a cage round a rotted host, foxfire and Grovekin burials inside, a hill of living canopy on its back. Rooted in phase 1, healed by the four heart-trees' lines (cut the Root Knots); it tears itself out at 50% and walks on its knuckles; in the hidden phase the heart-trees wake.

creatures.name: Gravehound
creatures._why: GY 2.12.1: a hairless hound at wolf-plus size with a greyhound's deep chest (the Xoloitzcuintli, the church grim): skin so thin and slate-dark the skull, spine ridge and ribs show; a bone-pale skull face; soul-green eyeshine. It sleeps buried in grave soil by day and rises at dusk (WRGraveCreatures); its Grim howl wakes every buried hound within 40 m.

creatures.name: Cryptstalker
creatures._why: GY 2.12.1: an amblypygid (whip spider) at 4 m leg span: flat, eyeless, whip-thin sensing front legs 5 m long that sweep the dark, spined raptorial palps that snap shut; runs sideways; clings to walls and ceilings in the catacombs and drops from above (WRGraveCreatures).

creatures.name: Wraithmoth
creatures._why: GY 2.12.1: a death's-head hawkmoth at 2.6 m span: the skull on its thorax faces you as it dives, swept ash-brown wings with a bruise-violet underwing, a tear-drinking proboscis. Drawn to the brightest light within 30 m; a dive puts out a torch; on a downed survivor it lands and drinks.

creatures.name: Palestrider
creatures._why: GY 2.12.1: a tall lean horse (an Akhal-Teke frame) in an ash-white coat, its face hairless and so thin-skinned the skull shows bone-pale (the Mari Lwyd), dark hollow nostrils, a long ragged black mane. Ridden it never tires (WRTaming); it rears at fire; its death scream turns the herd.

creatures.name: Tombback
creatures._why: GY 2.12.1: a burying beetle (Nicrophorus) 3 m long, black with rust-orange bands, a grave slab cemented to its back with its own wax. It buries carcasses under the slab; stopped, the slab is cover (600 HP); frontal blows land on the stone (x0.3) unless it rears (belly x1.3).

creatures.name: Gloamcrow
creatures._why: GY 2.12.1: a hooded crow with a jackdaw's pale eyes at raven size: black with an ash-grey hood, silver-white eyes. A group falls silent over any dead thing (the crow funeral) and mobs whatever killed it. Tamed it circles over secrets and full graves within 40 m and screams before you step on subsidence ground.

creatures.name: Mournhare
creatures._why: GY 2.12.1: a mountain hare in a grey coat, white belly, black ear tips; it sits up and moon-gazes at dusk; caught, it screams (real hares do). Gravecloth's fur.

creatures.name: Wickbeetle
creatures._why: GY 2.12.1: a 50 cm beetle whose back secretes white wax, a firefly light organ at its tail glowing candle-yellow: a walking candle. Tamed, a 12 m light no draught or rain puts out, and a wax every 20 minutes.

creatures.name: Marrowgoat
creatures._why: GY 2.12.1 (the 9th, added for Raven's 3/3/3): a shaggy chalk-white goat with horns sweeping back and down, gold eyes, a bone in its mouth: it gnaws old bones for their minerals (osteophagia). Milk, felt; a pen of them clears bone piles.

creatures.name: Risen mourner
creatures._why: A human skeleton in grave wrappings carrying a tōrō lantern on a pole (GY 2.12.4): the Mixamo rig's own clips drive bone parts on its bones (the body mesh hidden), grave-light threads at the joints.

creatures.name: Risen hound
creatures._why: A Gravehound's skeleton, grave-light in the sockets (GY 2.12.4).

creatures.name: Risen bearer
creatures._why: Two human skeletons fused at the shoulder carrying a coffin between them as a ram (GY 2.12.4): one rig, both bodies built on it.

creatures.name: The Bell-Ringer
creatures._why: The Belfry's sexton (the passing bell, the death knell; GY 2.13.1): a hunchback 4.2 m tall with arms to his knees, his head inside half a cracked bronze bell, a barrel-sized hand-bell at his belt. His Toll raises the yard's dead while the great bell's rope holds: cut its frayed section and he can't raise anything, and his stance breaks easily.

creatures.name: The Crypt Mother
creatures._why: A Cryptstalker with a 9 m leg span and 7 m whips (amblypygid mothers carry their young; GY 2.13.2), a living cloak of about 20 pale young on her flat back. Burn her eight egg sacs and nothing more hatches; fire on her back kills the riders.

creatures.name: Crypt Mother's young
creatures._why: The pale young off the Crypt Mother's back and out of her egg sacs (GY 2.13.2, combat 2.18.3 swarm): 40 HP, 8-damage bites, only ever out in her fight (WRGraveBosses hatches and sheds them).

creatures.name: The Ossuary Lord
creatures._why: A 6 m giant built from the bones of hundreds (Sedlec; GY 2.13.3): thigh bones bound into its limbs, ribcages stacked into its chest, a crown of skulls, three keystone skulls crusted in soulstone holding it together. It falls to a pile and re-forms; roots, quicklime or the three keystones smashed in the pile end it.

creatures.name: The Gravedigger
creatures._why: The resurrection men and the Mari Lwyd (GY 2.13.4): a gaunt figure 5.2 m tall in an oilskin coat, a horse skull under a white sheet for a head, a 2.5 m iron spade, a coffin-shaped mortsafe cage on his back with a lantern on a pole. Sleeps in the Watch House by day, digs graves on his round by night.

creatures.name: Nhal, the Last Mourner
creatures._why: A veiled mourner 9 m tall in the roofless Chapel of Nhal (GY 2.14): a woman's shape stretched too far, a crown of tōrō lantern-horns, a veil of thousands of roosting Wraithmoths, an 8 m scythe of black yew and bell bronze. She raises the dead from the chapel's twelve tombs; roots and heartwood stakes seal them. Weak to Nature.

creatures.name: Prismback
creatures._why: Crystal 2.12.1: a Komodo's heavy low body with a spine of tilted mirror-plates (scaly-foot snail mineral armour from licked crystal) that swing toward a bow draw or a cast and throw projectiles back from its plated flank (WRCrystalCreatures). Glare: plates tilted to the brightest light near it, into your eyes.

creatures.name: Spindleglass
creatures._why: Crystal 2.12.1: a harvestman's small clear body slung 3 m up between eight selenite-banded legs (9 m span); a glass frog's clear skin over a dark beating heart, clouding pink-grey when it hunts. It hunts by footsteps (vibration), never by sight; a broken leg falls and rings (WRCrystalCreatures).

creatures.name: Echobat
creatures._why: Crystal 2.12.1: an oilbird's clicks and screams on a ghost bat's pale body, 3 m across, ears as long as its head, a wrinkled leaf-nose. It hunts only what it hears (crystal.noise; x0.7 in rain in the upper halls) and goes deaf for 30 s in a Resonance peal (WRCrystalCreatures).

creatures.name: Geodemite
creatures._why: Crystal 2.12.1: an army ant at 40 cm with a honeypot ant's swollen abdomen gone to clear violet crystal. Columns pour out of nest geodes; a bite marks, four latched mark you in two seconds; they burst in shards when they die (WRCrystalCreatures).

creatures.name: Lumenhorn
creatures._why: Crystal 2.12.1: an Irish elk's build carrying a 3.2 m palmate spread of clear violet crystal over bone, glowing lilac-white (a rider's light, 15 m, steady and silent). The herd bellows when one is hit: a 40 m noise that flares every crystal and calls the Echobats.

creatures.name: Druseback
creatures._why: Crystal 2.12.1: a giant isopod the size of a cart, seven back segments each a split geode with violet crystal at the seam; it rolls into a ball when struck hard (damage x0.3) and breaks thin floors by walking.

creatures.name: Gemsniffer
creatures._why: Crystal 2.12.1: an aardvark's snout, ears and digging claws, an anteater's hook-claw stance, the carbunclo's glowing brow gem; tamed, its gem brightens and it points toward gems, amethyst, resonant crystal and caches within 20 m.

creatures.name: Alicanto
creatures._why: Crystal 2.12.1: a seriema's long legs and run, flightless, wings held open as it runs and glowing the colour of the metal it eats (silver-white). It dims and runs to the nearest drop edge when it sees you following; tamed, it leads to the richest ore within 40 m.

creatures.name: Chimecrab
creatures._why: Crystal 2.12.1: a coconut crab carrying the geode it grew into (basalt outside, violet druse in the open face); its shell rings when struck (a 10 m noise).

creatures.name: The Mirrored Twins
creatures._why: Wardcarver constructs guarding the Archive of Wards (crystal 2.13.1): a bronze armature cast by lost wax and grown over with resonant crystal into a knight 2.6 m tall, faceless hexafoil helm, crystal longsword and kite shield. There is only one: the other is its double, thrown by the Spar Lens in the ceiling. Only the real knight has a reflection in the water on the floor; every 12 s the lens turns and the two trade places. Three shots on the flaring lens shatter it.

creatures.name: The Mirrored Twins
creatures._why: The Spar Lens's second image of the real knight (crystal 2.13.1): hard light that hits as hard as the knight but takes no blow (weapons pass through it), and casts no reflection in the water. Spawned and driven only by the real knight (WRCrystalBosses); never in a den.

creatures.name: The Echo Warden
creatures._why: A blind bronze construct 5 m tall on four long heron legs before the Silent Vault's door (crystal 2.13.2), built to kill anything that makes a sound there: its head a great tuning fork, two flared ear-horns on its shoulders that swivel to every sound. It goes to the loudest noise within 30 m. A struck chime stone sends it to hammer the chime with its back to you; each breaks after three hammerings.

creatures.name: The Geode Tyrant
creatures._why: A Prismback the size of a house (crystal 2.13.3): 12 m long, 4.5 m at the shoulder, its plates whole split geodes 3 m tall, its hide scarred grey, one eye clouded white. It walks a round of the richest crystal from its hot-pool wallow under the Chandelier Gallery and up to the agate rinds. Its plates throw back every spell and shot; melee and the Void pass; a chandelier dropped on it, or a charge into a selenite beam, stuns it.

creatures.name: Lyrathis, the Prism Sovereign
creatures._why: The second of two crystal women the Wardcarvers grew in the Sovereigns' Mould to be living wards against the Void (crystal 2.14): her light, turned by eight prisms up eight shafts, shone over the Severance until her sister was hollowed; then she turned the prisms inward and raised her dome. A giantess 9 m tall in violet glass over a basalt core, a brow gem, a crown of eight spires, selenite needle hair that chimes, a heart crystal turning in her chest, blades of crystal from her wrists. Her beam splits through the prism nearest her; turn the prisms on their turntables to send it where you want it: onto her dome to break it, onto a wall to put out a copy.

creatures.name: Lyrathis, the Prism Sovereign
creatures._why: A refracted copy of Lyrathis (crystal 2.14.2, phase 2): light standing where the line from her through a prism meets open floor 15 m past the ring. It repeats her moves half a second later and takes no blow; turn its prism so the line meets a wall or another prism and it goes out. Spawned and moved only by her (WRCrystalLyrathis); never in a den.

creatures.name: Galeharrier
creatures._why: SKY 2.9: a harpy eagle's broad fingered wings at 2.8 m, a raised double crest tipped pale teal that flares before a stoop, a black hood with a white face-ring, slate back, white belly barred black, yellow feet too big for it with 7 cm talons. Pairs circle the W1 high islands and W3 by day and roost on the toll towers at night; a gliding survivor is its first pick; it robs Puffwings and anyone holding raw meat.

creatures.name: Skyray
creatures._why: SKY 2.9: a 9 m manta diamond, charcoal flecked pale above, white with black blotches below (each one's own), horn-lobes rolled at its mouth that unroll before the Undertow, a whip tail with a barb, a violet rim at night. It drifts 10-30 m off the W2 and W3 lips (lower in Overcast), and breaches out of the cloud in groups at dusk in a Gale. Tamed it's a sky raft (900 cm/s, 200 m over the ground at most, no fighting while it carries). Built in code (WRSkyBeast ray).

creatures.name: Cloudback
creatures._why: SKY 2.9: a 7 m whale floating 2 m up on the glowing levistone barnacles crusting its hump; grey-blue, white throat grooves, stubby fins, a fluke. Pods of 2-3 graze the W2 lagoons and gardens and sleep over the lagoons. Tamed it's a floating hauler (250 kg, it crosses gaps to 60 m). Offer it levistone. Built in code (WRSkyBeast whale).

creatures.name: Mistlark
creatures._why: SKY 2.9: a lark with long pointed wings and a fanned tail, soft grey and white with a mist-blue throat; flocks of 6-20 swirl like smoke in every updraft by day (a flock spinning up is a free lift) and roost in the cedars at night. Tamed it flies to and circles every column within 300 m: your eyes, no HUD.

creatures.name: Puffwing
creatures._why: SKY 2.9: a heavy, round flightless ground bird (a takahē) 0.9 m tall, moss-green back, blue breast, a red bill and frontal shield, oversized soft wings with white glider-grade under-feathers that it spreads to parachute off an edge when scared. Flocks of 3-6 on the W1 turf and the W2 gardens; burrows at night; its boom from the rookery at dusk. Feathers and eggs.

creatures.name: Gallowshrike
creatures._why: SKY 2.9: upright and long-legged, 2.2 m: a shrike's head with a black bandit mask and a hooked beak with a tomial tooth, short stiff black wings it spreads to hop-glide between islands, a 12 cm black dagger claw on each inner toe; ash-grey, white throat, rust-red under the tail. Packs of 2-4 on Larder Isle, the W2 edges and Kite Barrow, hunting at dusk and dawn, sleeping in their larder trees; a fresh kill on a thorn means a pack within 60 m. You hear the rattle before you see them.

creatures.name: Hushwing
creatures._why: SKY 2.9: owl-broad round wings with soft fringed edges at 5 m, a flat frogmouth head that splits open into a gape wider than itself, huge forward eyes with amber shine, bark-brown and moon-grey mottling that vanishes against cloud, a pale facial disc that flashes white as it strikes. Silent: its only sound is the churr. Night above 700 m; by day the Undercloud roost and the Weeping Isle's third cave (in Cloud fog it hunts by day). It takes a Windmane foal with no adult within 30 m.

creatures.name: Sailbell
creatures._why: SKY 2.9: a translucent clear-blue gas float with a raised violet crest-sail and a curtain of fine tentacles hanging 12 m with violet beads that glow at night; it drifts at 45 degrees to the wind (left-handed bells one side, right-handed the other: the man o' war), so one bloom tells you where the next crosses a bridge. Beautiful from far, horrible close: the curtain holds half-digested Mistlarks. Dead by anything but fire it deflates and its curtain stings for 60 s more. Tamed (from a bud) and tethered it stings anything hostile within 10 m: a living fence. Built in code (WRSkyBeast bell).

creatures.name: Kyrra, the Tempest Harrier
creatures._why: SKY 2.10: a Galeharrier hen grown to 9 m across, her crest white with age, one talon a stump bound in old Kitewright chain. She hunts the bridges on a 2.4 km loop over W3 (Tollgate to Brink and back over Eyrie Rock), landing every 6 min on the widest island on her way for 60 s to scan. Arrows to the wings ground her (each wing 250 stance, ranged x2): 10 s down, damage x1.25; both broken, she fights on foot to the end.

creatures.name: The Bridge Sentinel
creatures._why: SKY 2.10: a Kitewright guardian 6 m tall of white granite, a halo of eight stone wind-vanes behind its head that turn as it walks and sing like an aeolian harp (heard 80 m off); it pries up deck stones to throw. On the standing bridge from Tollgate to Span North; lair the Toll House. Lure its Vane slam onto a weak section: it falls 35 m to Winch Isle, takes a quarter of its health and kneels 10 s.

creatures.name: Old Gulper
creatures._why: SKY 2.10: a Cloudback grown to 22 m, mean and half-blind, its hump a reef of levistone barnacles, scarred with old harpoon wounds. It floats over Gulper's Bight and inhales anything near. Feed it a fire hit, a lit fire pot or a thrown torch while it inhales: it chokes, sinks onto the lagoon with its mouth open for 10 s (x1.5); two chokes in 60 s crack its hump. Built in code (WRSkyBeast whale).

creatures.name: Aeolith, the Sky Serpent
creatures._why: SKY 2.11: the feathered wind serpent the Kitewrights bound to circle the Flue and blow the Deepfarmers' spores back down: 60 m, 2.2 m thick at the chest, one pair of feathered wings 34 m across set behind the head like a cobra's hood, a bone wind-mask on its snout, a jaw that opens 120 degrees, a red throat sac that swells before every breath (it glows at night), quetzal plumes along its spine and a 6 m tail fan. Jade-teal scales to an ivory belly; ivory feathers tipped jade and gold. Built in code (WRSkyBeast serpent).
